title: A chromone-based Schiff base derivative for the Cd 2+ -promoted detection of  l -proline: validated by DFT, test strip, cotton swab, fish tissue, cellular imaging, and real/herbal water recovery analysis
content: l-proline is a vital stress marker in plants and an indicator of food quality and clinical diagnosis. In this work, we applied a simple chromone-based Schiff base derivative, (E)-3-(((3-mercapto-5-phenyl-4H-1,2,4-triazol-4-yl)imino)methyl)-4H-chromen-4-one (CT), for the Cd2+-complex-promoted detection of l-proline in acetonitrile. Within 10 minutes of incubation, the CT–Cd2+ complex exhibited a strong PL “Turn-On” response in the presence of l-proline among the amino acids, which remained stable between pH 3 and 8. The Job's plot and 1H NMR (nuclear magnetic resonance)-based titration studies confirmed the 1 : 1 stoichiometry of CT + Cd2+ to l-proline. Between 0.1 µM and 300 µM, the PL linear dynamic range of CT + Cd2+ to l-proline was observed, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 141 nM and an association constant (Ka) of 4.25 × 103 M−1 using the Benesi–Hildebrand plot. The mode of binding and the possible photoinduced electron transfer/fluorescence resonance energy transfer (PET/FRET) mechanism are defined by FTIR spectroscopy, 1H NMR, HR mass spectrometry, and density functional theory (DFT) studies. l-proline sensing by the Cd2+ complex-promoted technique is corroborated using a test strip, cotton swab, fish tissue, and A549/MCF-7 cellular imaging. l-proline recovery from tap water and herbal water extracts (including Astragalus root (AA), Hedysari root (NAAI), and Coastal Glehnia root (SGC)) ranged from 89.89% to 113.98%. This unique design drives future innovation for l-proline monitoring in biological and environmental samples.
